key: Then We gave the Scripture as inheritance unto those whom We elected of Our bondmen. But of them are some who wrong themselves and of them are some who are lukewarm, and of them are some who outstrip (others) through good deeds, by Allah’s leave.
s: After the Prophet’s Scripture is said to confirm what came before, the ayah sorts its heirs into three; al-Tabari, on 35:32, reads the one who wrongs himself as guilty of sins short of hypocrisy and idolatry, since the Gardens promised next include all three.

evidence.gloss: As for the one who wrongs himself, that he be of the people of sins and disobedience that fall below hypocrisy and associating partners with God is, in my view, closer to the sense of the ayah than that he be the hypocrite or the disbeliever; for God, exalted be His mention, followed this ayah with His saying “Gardens of Eden, they enter them”, and so took in all three kinds with entry into the Garden.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Fatir 35:32, at 3691; ends before “That is the great favour!”). Al-Tabari reports two camps: the one who wrongs himself is a sinner of this community who is forgiven (Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud, Ka’b), or the hypocrite bound for the Fire (al-Hasan, Qatada, Ikrima, Mujahid). In his own voice (“عندي”) he holds the sinner short of hypocrisy and shirk closer to the ayah’s sense, because 35:33 extends entry into the Gardens to all three kinds. The sentence paraphrases this without adding his separate point that the Scripture means the earlier books. Plain sense: 35:31 says the Scripture inspired to the Prophet confirms what came before, and 35:32 divides the heirs into three, faithful to day.js. 44 words; entry-check ok.
